mistake_one.title: Matching every wood tone in the room
mistake_one.body: A kitchen where the floor, the cabinetry and the table are all the same timber reads as a showroom set rather than a room that was put together over time. Matched tones flatten the depth that made you want wood in the first place: everything sits on one plane, nothing recedes, and the warmth you were buying goes flat under the lights.
mistake_one.fix: Keep one piece deliberately older and darker than the rest. A table or a run of open shelving a few shades past the floor gives the eye somewhere to land, and the mismatch reads as age rather than as a mistake.

mistake_one.title: Solving a storage problem with more cabinetry
mistake_one.body: The instinct in a minimal kitchen is to add another run of units so that nothing has to sit out. It works for about a month. Full cupboards turn every door into a decision, and the room stops feeling calm long before it stops being tidy — the clear surfaces you wanted are the first thing to go.
mistake_one.fix: Plan one drawer you never fill. Deliberate slack is what keeps the counters clear a year in; a kitchen packed to its capacity has nowhere to put the ordinary mess of a Tuesday, so the mess stays on the worktop.

mistake_one.title: Buying anything pre-distressed
mistake_one.body: Factory wear is printed, and printed wear repeats. Once you have noticed the same scratch on two cabinet fronts you cannot stop noticing it, and the room drops from raw to themed in a single look. This style reads as honest only while the marks look earned.
mistake_one.fix: Buy plain and let the room do the ageing. Unfinished steel, mill-finish hardware and oiled rather than lacquered timber all mark unevenly inside a year — which is the look the distressed version is imitating and never quite gets.

mistake_one.title: Mixing more than two metals
mistake_one.body: Taps, handles, hinges, lighting and the rail on the range are five separate chances to introduce a finish. Past two, a classic kitchen loses the quiet coordination the whole style depends on and starts reading as a collection of separate purchases that happened to end up in one room.
mistake_one.fix: Pick two and hold the line — brass carries the warmth, nickel does the working parts. Anything black is a third metal whatever the showroom calls it, and it is the one that dates fastest.
